target_customer: Mobile app developers building native iOS and Android apps
problem: Shipping changes to native mobile apps meant waiting on app store review and there was no easy way to A/B test. Clutch offered native A/B testing plus a framework for faster hybrid native and HTML iteration.
business_model: Hosted developer service (A/B testing SDK), pricing not found

founders.name: Eric Florenzano
previous_startups: Convore (co-founder and CTO; defunct YC company per TheNextWeb)
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Eric Maguire
founders.background_notes: Named by TheNextWeb (2012) as co-founder; not on the YC page I read.

exit.reason: Twitter said it acquired the intellectual property; team joined its Growth and International group, hosted service closed 2012-11-01 and code was open sourced

technical_complexity.rationale: Required SDKs for native iOS and Android that could swap experiment variants at runtime, plus a backend; standard engineering with some hard parts around native integration.

defensibility.rationale: An SDK plus dashboard that others could copy, and Twitter later open-sourced the code.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twitter acquired the team and IP in August 2012 and shut the hosted service.

market_need_then: App store review delays made native app iteration slow; YC and Twitter both saw value, though no customer or revenue numbers were found.

branding.domain_note: The clutch.io domain is now used by an unrelated agentic website company (fetched 2026).

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found; the name is shared by many unrelated companies, which swamps search results.

outcome_analysis: Clutch was a two person YC Summer 2011 team that launched publicly around early 2012, then was bought by Twitter in August 2012 for its IP and people. Twitter closed the hosted service on November 1, 2012 and open sourced the code, which makes it an acquihire with no continued product. Price and funding are not public.
notes: clutch.io now hosts an unrelated company, so the original site was effectively dead. Funding search returned only unrelated companies named Clutch; no rounds recorded, coverage none_found. Launch about April 2012 from a Hacker News post snippet. Competitor search found only Leanplum mentioned in an August 2012 HN thread (after the batch), so the list is empty. Success factor is weak; acquihire reading from TechCrunch headline snippets and the company's own announcement.
